Hi Helen — thanks for sending these over and for the context.

Short checklist (what we need from Skylift to create a vendor record and accept POs):
- Legal entity name exactly as on W-9/W-8: Skylift AI, Inc.
- Remittance / invoicing email and AP contact (name, email, phone)
- Bank details for wire transfers (routing/account) OR confirmation you accept net30 via marketplace billing
- Preferred billing path: (a) Marketplace-managed subscriptions (AWS/GCP billing) OR (b) Redwood invoice against PO
- Copy of signed standard purchasing terms if you have them (optional)
- For EU sales: VAT registration form or W-8 if non-US entity (flagging for Vanessa)

Operational notes:
- If you choose Redwood invoice against PO, invoice must include PO number in the invoice header; our accounting systems reject invoices without it.
- Payment terms default to NET30 unless otherwise negotiated and reflected in the PO.
- For marketplace-billed customers, AWS/GCP handle payment collection; Redwood invoices are rarely used in that flow.

Next steps: please complete our vendor-intake form (link below) and attach a copy of your bank details if you want wires enabled. After we receive those, our finance ops team (Marcus) will create the vendor record and confirm a vendor ID.

Vendor intake form: https://app.redwood.com/vendor-intake/form/9f3a2

I’m copying Vanessa for tax/procurement routing notes.

Thanks,

Hi Helen / team — adding some practical routing guidance from our side: 

1) Marketplace vs Redwood invoice: 
- AWS Marketplace: For paid listings we typically provision via the AWS SaaS Marketplace metering/subscription model. In that case, AWS issues invoices to the end-customer and pays Redwood; Skylift will receive settlement from AWS according to their schedule. No PO is required to be submitted to Redwood for those flows.
- GCP Marketplace: similar model for subscriptions, but if the buyer prefers to issue POs we can also accept Redwood invoices (requires vendor setup).

2) Required docs to finalize vendor record (minimum):
- Completed vendor-intake form (link provided by Nikhil)
- W-9 (we have it) or W-8 BEN-E if non-US
- Bank details for ACH/wire (CSV or bank letter)
- Preferred remittance method and AP contact info

3) PO handling rules: 
- Invoices without a valid PO number will be routed back to vendor — this creates fulfillment delays.
- If you expect PO issuance from customers to Skylift (and Skylift will route to Redwood), ensure the PO references Redwood vendor ID once we create it; otherwise accounting will not map the invoice.

4) International/tax notes (if Skylift will sell to EU customers):
- We'll need VAT registration (if applicable) and a remit address for EU invoices. For EU-pass-through, billing to the buyer may require different invoice fields.

Once you submit bank details through the intake form, we can flip the internal switch and enable PO acceptance. Marcus: can you confirm expected turnaround for vendor creation once intake is complete?

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace Program Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
